svg.title: Order management system: database design
svg.text: Polyglot persistence: one store per access pattern. Postgres is the source of truth, everything else is a derived view.
Source of truth: orders, payments, inventory
written in the same txn as order
WHAT TO SAY IN THE INTERVIEW
ACID source of truth for orders, payments, inventory; strong consistency
Normalized schema + FKs; index access paths (user_id, created_at DESC)
MVCC; row lock (SELECT FOR UPDATE) or optimistic version on stock
Idempotency key UNIQUE on payments: safe retries, no double charge
Transactional outbox + CDC (Debezium) → Kafka → Cassandra, ES, ClickHouse
Scale reads: replicas (async lag), PgBouncer; partition orders by month
Scale writes: shard by user_id (Citus / app-level) only when needed
else return -1 end -- out of stock, no oversell
WHAT TO SAY IN THE INTERVIEW
Cluster mode: 16,384 hash slots; replicas per shard for failover
Eviction policy: LRU / LFU / FIFO / TTL
Cache stampede: request coalescing, cache warm-up
Cache consistency: invalidation, short TTL, eventual consistency
Hot keys: replicate hot keys, application (local) cache, rate limiter
Lua scripts: atomic check + update in one round trip; short, same-slot keys
Order history at scale: write-heavy, query-first
HOW DATA IS STORED: ONE TABLE PER QUERY
PRIMARY KEY ((user_id, month_bucket), created_at DESC, order_id)
Partition (u_42, 2026-10): rows sorted on disk by created_at DESC
Partition (order 9f1): events stored in time order
WHAT TO SAY IN THE INTERVIEW
High write throughput: LSM tree (commit log → memtable → SSTable)
Predictable access pattern: one table per query
Consistent hashing ring + virtual nodes; gossip protocol
Tunable consistency: R + W > N; RF = 3, LOCAL_QUORUM
Wide-column database; Bloom filter per SSTable skips disk reads
Tombstones + compaction; time-bucket keys avoid unbounded partitions
PK = user_id (+ bucket), clustering = created_at DESC; no joins / ad-hoc queries
WHAT TO SAY IN THE INTERVIEW
Full-text search, fuzzy search; filtering, ranking, aggregations; auto-complete
Text analysis → inverted index creation → BM25 relevance scoring
Derived from Postgres via CDC: eventually consistent, rebuildable
PARTITION BY month · ORDER BY (order_date, category_id)
WHAT TO SAY IN THE INTERVIEW
Columnar OLAP: reads only needed columns, high compression, fast aggregations
Append-only batch inserts from Kafka; not for OLTP, no frequent row updates
Use for: revenue by day / category, funnels, dashboards over billions of rows
How the stores stay in sync
Redis in front of reads: cache-aside, cart, session, stock counters, idempotency
Write: API → Postgres txn (order + outbox) → CDC → Kafka → consumers
Consistency: strong in Postgres, eventual everywhere else
